They continuously analyze service health trends, investigate deviations early (good or bad), and drive disciplined, root-cause-based improvement. They are comfortable asking hard questions, raising risks early and transparently, and challenging engineering to prove operational readiness before new services go live. Analyze platform metrics and raw operational data to spot emerging risks and trends, open early investigations into anomalies, lead structured root cause analysis, and drive critical issues to resolution quickly. Ensure 24/7 service reliability through disciplined incident, problem and change management consistent with mature SRE organizations. Set and enforce production readiness standards: no new service or feature is approved without documentation, monitoring plans, alerting thresholds, runbooks, security review and capacity planning. Partner with, and constructively challenge, Engineering and Product on architecture, scalability assumptions and monitoring strategy. Provide executive-level updates on operational status, current work and next steps, raising risks early with data-backed assessments and recommended mitigations. Implement and oversee modern monitoring and log ingestion, including AI-powered log analysis, using tools such as NetScout and Datadog, with meaningful budget behind the effort. Manage and optimize cloud infrastructure across AWS and Azure, balancing performance, availability, security and cost. Lead Corporate IT and Security: policy development, access controls, endpoint management, application curation and system lockdown, regulatory compliance, vulnerability management and risk mitigation. Establish ITIL/ITSM-aligned service management across enterprise SaaS platforms (Salesforce, Azure DB, collaboration tools and more), and formalize internal process, procedure, logging and data practices. Experience leading or working within SRE, NOC or production operations teams with direct accountability for uptime, incident response and SLA performance. Proven ability to design and implement observability frameworks: metrics, alerting, logging and performance dashboards. Experience implementing structured change management and production readiness reviews to prevent service disruption. Experience overseeing Corporate IT and Security, including compliance frameworks such as CCPA, CPNI, FCC (Title 47, Part 64), PCI, NIST or similar. Strong analytical, budgeting and financial management skills, balancing cost discipline with operational resilience. Executive presence and polished communication: able to influence decisions with data-driven reasoning, challenge engineering decisions, and keep a collaborative but appropriately skeptical relationship with technical teams. Discretion, sound judgment under pressure, and the ability to maintain confidentiality. Willingness to work flexible hours as needed to support production operations. Preferred Experience with modern monitoring and log ingestion tools such as NetScout and Datadog. Familiarity with AI and machine learning tools for operational visibility and log analysis. AWS infrastructure experience. Experience implementing security lockdown and application curation. ITIL certification or equivalent experience. Functional knowledge of contact center technologies (Salesforce, Jira, InContact or similar). Why This Role Transform platform reliability from 99.9% to five nines (99.999%), a major, visible operational improvement. Authority to implement modern monitoring and AI-powered log ingestion with a substantial annual tooling budget. Lead a large, diverse team of about 40 across multiple critical infrastructure domains, with the autonomy to evaluate and reshape the management structure. To keep collaboration smooth across our distributed team, we ask for at least 3 hours of daily overlap with US Central Time. You’ll also take part in an on-call rotation, with shifts scheduled during your own local hours so coverage fits around your day. The Company You’ll Join Amperon is the leading energy forecasting company, positioned at the intersection of energy data and AI. Founded in 2018, Amperon has become a trusted partner for power and utility companies, delivering demand, renewable generation, and price forecasts. With cutting-edge predictive analytics, seamless data integrations, and premium customer support, Amperon enables customers to enhance grid reliability and optimize asset performance. Committed to grid modernization, Amperon is the forecasting company of the energy transition. We bring the brightest minds together across energy, software engineering, AI and ML, and SaaS to accelerate the energy transition and deliver value to our energy market participants every day. Our Strategy Amperon seeks to modernize the grid data and AI software stack to improve reliability, optimize asset economics, and accelerate decarbonization for grid operators, asset owners, and end-users. We're building the next generation of market-leading energy analytics and forecasting products, and we want you to be part of our journey! About The Role We're hiring a Staff Cloud Platform Engineer to own major parts of the Azure and Kubernetes platform that runs Amperon's product, data pipelines and growing set of AI agents. You'll join our small Infrastructure & Security team, working across infrastructure, site reliability and security, and reporting to the Director of Infrastructure & Security. This is a hands-on, senior individual-contributor role. Everyone on the team shares ownership of the platform and the on-call. As a Staff engineer, you'll set technical direction for whole areas of it, lead multi-month programs from design to cutover, and raise the bar for how the rest of engineering builds and runs software. Amperon's people work from 17 countries across the Americas, Europe and the Middle East, so someone is on hand during the working day for our customers and for the engineering teams we support. We hire for one global team and welcome candidates in UK, EU or US time zones. What You’ll Do Shape our Kubernetes platform. Run and evolve several AKS clusters (production, workflow, and AI/agent workloads) with Karpenter, Cilium network policy, workload identity, External Secrets, Helm and ArgoCD. Lead infrastructure-as-code at scale. Drive our Terraform estate, run through Atlantis: provider upgrades, drift reconciliation, module design and guardrails that keep changes safe, plus the GitHub Actions runners and build pipelines that ship them. Make our data stores resilient. Our customers depend on forecasts every hour, so reliable data is core to the product. Operate MySQL Flexible Server and self-managed ClickHouse with resilience first: replication, failover, backup and restore, capacity planning and safe upgrades. Build the platform for AI agents. Design isolated, auditable environments for agentic workloads and MCP services, including egress controls, identity and observability, and a self-service path for teams to deploy internal apps safely. Make the platform observable. Evolve our observability stack (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Tempo), keep alert rules in code, and make sure we hear about problems before customers do. Manage cloud cost. Find and land Azure savings; we have cut tens of thousands of dollars a month and expect more. Share the operational load. Join an on-call rotation spread across time zones, so customers and our own engineering teams get help during their working hours. Lead incident response and blameless postmortems, and support data engineering, data science and product teams. Multiply the team. Write design docs, review code, mentor engineers, and leave systems documented so no one person is a single point of failure. We Think This Role Would Be A Great Fit If You Have 8+ years in infrastructure, platform or site reliability engineering, including several years at a senior level owning production systems. A track record of leading multi-month infrastructure programs end to end: design doc, stakeholder alignment, phased rollout, cutover and cleanup. Deep, hands-on Kubernetes experience in production, ideally on a managed offering (AKS, EKS or GKE), including networking and network policy. Strong Terraform skills on a large codebase, with GitOps-style workflows (Atlantis, ArgoCD or similar). Production experience with at least one major cloud. Azure is strongly preferred; deep AWS or GCP experience with a willingness to go deep on Azure also works. Experience operating relational or analytical databases in production (MySQL, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse or similar), including replication, upgrades and recovery. Security built into how you work: least privilege, identity-based access over static credentials, secrets management, and network isolation. Solid observability practice: metrics, logs and traces (ideally with OpenTelemetry), alerting that people trust, and SLO thinking. Comfortable writing Python and shell for automation and tooling. Clear written communication. Much of our work happens in design docs, PRs and async threads across time zones. Additional Nice to Haves Running ClickHouse at scale, including clustering and replication. Argo Workflows or other high-volume batch and workflow platforms. Cilium, Karpenter or Node Auto Provisioning on AKS. Infrastructure for AI agents or LLM workloads: sandboxing, egress controls, model gateways, Azure AI Foundry. Using AI coding agents (such as Claude Code) as a daily part of your engineering work. Compliance programs such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001. Cloud cost management (FinOps) on Azure. Experience in energy, utilities or time-series data platforms. Benefits & Perks While we are serious about our company's culture, we aren't going to force "culture" to prove that we are cool and fun. It’s a company filled with smart, genuinely nice individuals who are passionate about data science, energy and working together to build a product that can have a lasting impact on our planet. Even though we are a remote company with employees spread across the globe, we still believe human interaction is a good thing. We will also have an all-company event at least once a year so people can get to know each other in a more fun and social way. Competitive salary plus stock option package. Based on geographical location. Medical, dental and vision insurance Annual company retreat Flexible PTO policy (take what you need) Flexible working If you are excited about contributing to a product that can have a lasting impact on our planet and you thrive in fast-paced, innovative environments, we would love to hear from you.

review_candidates.description: About Allica Bank Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech. Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers. Department Description Platform Engineering is the centralised team that builds, provisions and runs the infrastructure every other engineering team at Allica depends on. Whether a product serves a business banking customer or a colleague inside the bank, it lands on a platform this team designed. The team owns both halves of that, building the platform and running it, against the availability and resilience standards a regulated bank is held to. Well-architected is the operating standard, not an aspiration: reliability, security, cost and operational excellence are design inputs from the start. The job is to make the right thing the easy thing, through paved roads, self-service provisioning, sensible defaults, and controls encoded in the platform rather than bolted on afterwards. Every control the platform enforces is one a product team does not have to think about, and one we can evidence on demand. Role Description The Lead Platform Engineer is the senior technical leader for a core domain of Allica's platform. You set its technical direction, you are accountable for how it behaves in production, and you build it yourself. This is a hands-on role. Expect to spend a real share of your week in infrastructure as code, pipelines and live systems, and the rest setting standards, reviewing designs and making the calls that are too consequential to delegate. Your customers are internal. Product engineering and data engineering choose whether to use what you build, so adoption and the friction you remove are the measures that matter. Principal Accountabilities Platform Architecture and Engineering Own the architecture of Allica’s Cloud platform: landing zones, subscriptions and network topology, container runtime, and the integration and resilience patterns that sit on top. Design again Cloud Adoption Framework and Well-Architected Framework as working disciplines.  Build the reusable core: Terraform modules, deployment templates and platform services that let a team stand up production-grade infrastructure without reinventing the security, networking and observability plumbing each time. Infrastructure as Code and Automation  Deliver and manage all infrastructure through Terraform and secure CI/CD, so that every change is automated, repeatable, version-controlled, tested, and reversible. Drive manual change and configuration drift towards zero.  Set and evolve engineering standards for the function: code quality, peer review, policy as code and, release management. Security, Governance, and Compliance  Embed security, governance, and compliance throughout the platform lifecycle, implementing effective policies, access controls, encryption, vulnerability management, monitoring, and configuration standards.  Collaborate with Allica’s Security, Engineering, Risk, and Compliance teams to ensure platforms meet organisational, regulatory, and control requirements, supported by clear documentation and auditable evidence.  Identify and manage architectural risks, security vulnerabilities, control gaps, and technical debt, ensuring remediation actions are prioritised, tracked, and completed. Platform Operations and Service Ownership  Own availability, reliability, and run cost for the platform, backed by service objectives, monitoring you can operate from, and tested recovery arrangements. Lead the response to complex incidents, own the root-cause analysis, drive out repeat causes rather than repeat fixes.  Use service data, operational experience, and FinOps practices to continuously improve platform automation, resilience, engineering standards, cost visibility, forecasting, and resource optimisation. Team Leadership  Lead, mentor, and develop a team of platform engineers while remaining personally hands-on in architecture, design reviews, and the hardest technical problems.  Set the technical bar and raise it, through coaching, design review and the example of your own work. Personal Attributes & Experience  A strong track record architecting, and running production Azure environments at scale. Fluent in landing zone and subscription design, private networking, containerised compute, API management and resilience patterns across zones and regions. Line Management Experience Extensive hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure at scale, infrastructure as code, containerised runtimes, identity and observability.  Has carried production accountability for systems that matter. Comfortable in handling incidents.  Treats developer experience as a product. Talks to engineering teams, watches how they actually work and designs for adoption rather than mandate.  Treats regulatory and security requirements as engineering constraints to design around, not obstacles to route past. Prior regulated or high-assurance experience helps but is not a prerequisite.  Gets adoption by building things engineers want to use and by making a clear case, not by escalation.  Prefers the boring, well-understood solution unless the problem genuinely demands otherwise. Willing to remove things. Desirable Experience  Architecture or engineering experience with Google Cloud Platform.  Experience working in complex, regulated, or security-sensitive environments. Knowledge of Kubernetes, container platforms, serverless services, and cloud-native application patterns.  Experience with Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or comparable CI/CD technologies.  Familiarity with FinOps, operational resilience, regulatory compliance, and cloud-control frameworks.  Relevant Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Terraform, security, or architecture certifications. Advise developers on branching strategy, code review practice, versioning, and release management.
